[MUTATION ANALYSIS] A gene undergoes a single base deletion near the beginning of its coding sequence. 1) Predict the likely consequence of this deletion on the structure and function of the resulting protein. 2) Compare this outcome with a single base substitution mutation occurring at the exact same position.
rubric: To score full points, the structural analysis must state: 1) The single base deletion causes a frame shift mutation. This shifts the reading frame of all subsequent triplet codes, completely altering the downstream amino acid sequence and usually resulting in a non-functional protein. 2) A base substitution only changes a single triplet code at that position. It might change just one amino acid, create an early stop signal, or have no effect at all due to the degenerate nature of the genetic code, making a substitution generally less disruptive to the overall protein structure than a deletion frame shift.
